Anya: quick heads-up — profiler flagged a regression w/ fp8_fast kernel + KV rescale on long contexts (seen as NaNs / Inf after ~1k tokens). attaching minimal trace below.

Sam: ugh. repro steps? which model + config did this hit in canary?

Anya: repro on rdw/gpt-medium-14b-8k locally. config snippet: 
```
kernel_selector: auto
quant_profile: fp8_fast
kv_rescale: enabled
max_seq: 8192
batching: auto
```
observed when we hit a mix of single-token and long-prefix requests (continuous batching spikes).

Jorge: paste from logs: 
```
2026-03-16T21:12:02Z [INFER] dispatch -> fp8_fast selected for layer 19, seq=1056, kv_shape=(bs=1,seq=1056)
2026-03-16T21:12:02Z [NUMERIC] pre-gemm scale=1.2e-3 post-gemm=nan
2026-03-16T21:12:02Z [INFER] fallback -> kernel switch to fp8_safe triggered
```
noticed the pre-gemm scale ratio sometimes > 1e3 after rescale step.

Dana: thanks. hypothesis: rescale + fp8_fast kernel uses narrower accumulator path and doesn't clamp intermediate, so overflow -> NaN. two immediate mitigations: clamp scales after rescale, and add a safety heuristic in kernel selector to avoid fp8_fast when kv_scale_ratio > 1e2.

Sam: can we dump the kv cache scales distribution from the runtime for that trace? want to confirm the ratio across heads.

Jorge: posted a quick Python dump: 
```python
scales = runtime.get_kv_scales(layer=19)
min, max = min(scales), max(scales)
# result: 1.1e-5, 1.5e-1 -> ratio ~1.4e4
```
so yeah, huge spread across tokens/heads.

Dana: that explains it. options ranked: 1) clamp per-head scales to [1e-4, 1e1] post-rescale (cheap), 2) run smoothquant-style per-tensor calibration during upload (bigger change), 3) route to fp8_safe or int8 kernel for pathological KV shapes, 4) change batching heuristic to avoid mixing very short and very long sequences in same microbatch.

Anya: prefer 1+3 for a fast patch. clamp + kernel-selector rule: if kv_scale_ratio > 1e3 -> force fp8_safe or int8_fallback.

perf-bot: perf regression estimate — local microbench:
- before clamp (fp8_fast): 1.0x perf, but 0.7% NaN events on long seqs
- after clamp + selector -> fp8_safe fallback for 0.6% traffic: effective perf 0.93x overall, NaN -> 0
- int8_fallback perf ≈ 0.85x but stable

Sam: sounds good. action items: 
- Jorge: patch kernel selector rule + unit tests (ensure route when kv_scale_ratio>1e3)
- Dana: add quick clamp in rescale path + numeric assert (log first 10 clamps)
- Anya: run Canary rollout at 10% with perf gating and NaN monitor alerting

Jorge: i'll open PR for selector change and a small e2e test that simulates scale spread.

Anya: adding runbook notes: under incidents/quant-safety — immediate rollback: disable fp8_fast in canary.

Sam: :thumbsup: keep the messages short if you update the PR, and paste the perf numbers here.

Dana: one follow-up — we should add an offline calibration job that computes per-model smoothquant clamps and stores them in model metadata. put that in Optimize backlog.

perf-bot: scheduled canary: 2026-03-17T02:00:00Z -> 10% / 1h. will auto-rollback on >0 NaN events per minute.

Anya: thanks everyone — moving to implement.
